title: Case: International parcel has produced four out-for-delivery notices and no delivery
context: A recipient is waiting for an international parcel, DL-958, that arrived in the country at the end of June. He has stayed home on each day the carrier notified him it was out for delivery.
initial_request: Notice number four has landed. 'Out for delivery today.' I have now spent four days of annual leave watching a van not arrive, which is not how I pictured my summer. Before I ring work and burn a fifth: is it on a van today or isn't it? A yes or a no will do.

events.body: Third 'out for delivery today' text for DL-958, third day sat at home, third evening with no parcel. I rang the number: a robot, then eventually a person who read me the same tracking page I already had open. Could someone who can see more than I can have a look?
DL-958: the recipient has had out-for-delivery notices on 07-06, 07-07 and 07-08 and no delivery or attempt. Where is the parcel physically, and was it loaded on any of those days?

DL-958 is in the import hold cage, bay C, and has been since 06-29. It has an import hold flag against it so it cannot be loaded. It has not been on a van on any of those dates. The out-for-delivery texts go when the route plan is built overnight; the parcel then drops off the load list at the cage check in the morning. Import billing set and lift that flag. We can't.

The depot tell me DL-958 has not been on a van on any of those three days. It is being held at the depot under an import hold, and the notices were generated automatically from the route plan. I'm sorry: that is three days you were told to wait in for nothing. Have you had any request for import charges on it?
Import charge was paid online on 06-30, receipt IMP-958-R, I have the email. Nobody has asked me for anything since.
DL-958: the recipient says import charges were paid on 06-30, receipt IMP-958-R. Is anything outstanding on this shipment?
DL-958: charges paid in full 06-30, nothing outstanding. No hold from our side. As far as billing is concerned the parcel is released for delivery.

events.to: Lorcan Meadowcroft, recipient; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: DL-958 is out for delivery today between 08:00 and 18:00. Please make sure someone is available to receive it.

Notice number four has landed. 'Out for delivery today.' I have now spent four days of annual leave watching a van not arrive, which is not how I pictured my summer. Before I ring work and burn a fifth: is it on a van today or isn't it? A yes or a no will do.

acceptable_actions.summary: Put Import billing's 'paid, no hold, released' against the depot's hold flag and ask whether the flag is still on DL-958 and whether it is actually loaded today.
Tell Import billing the depot reported a hold flag on DL-958 that has kept it in the cage since 06-29 despite payment on 06-30, and ask them to check and lift it and confirm to the depot.

must: Sets the two statements side by side for the team it writes to: Import billing say charges were paid on 06-30 with no hold and the parcel released; the Destination depot say an import hold flag has kept DL-958 in the cage since 06-29 and it has never been loaded.
Asks for the contradiction to be settled, including whether DL-958 is physically on a van today given this morning's notice.
Says the recipient has taken four days off work on four notices and is deciding this morning whether to take a fifth, so an answer is needed quickly.
must_not: Tells Lorcan the parcel is out for delivery today or that he should stay in, on the strength of the notification.
Tells Lorcan the parcel has been released or will definitely be delivered on a given day, on the strength of Import billing's reply alone.
Tells Lorcan charges are still owed or asks him to pay or prove payment again.
Sends Lorcan a stock reply that tracking shows out for delivery and to allow until 18:00.
expected.reference_message: Urgent, DL-958. Yesterday at 11:45 you told me this parcel has been in the import hold cage, bay C, since 06-29 with an import hold flag, and has never been loaded. At 16:15 Import billing told me the charges were paid in full on 06-30, there is no hold from their side and the parcel is released. This morning at 06:58 the recipient received a fourth out-for-delivery notice. Those three things cannot all be right. Could you check now whether the hold flag is still showing against DL-958 on your system, and whether the parcel is physically on a van today or still in the cage? If the flag is still there, please say so plainly so I can take it back to Import billing. The recipient has taken four days off work for four notices and is deciding this morning whether to take a fifth.

rationale: Three sources disagree: the notification says out for delivery, the depot's last word was an import hold that prevents loading, and Import billing say there is no hold. None of them has been checked against the others since billing replied, so the desk cannot give the yes or no the recipient wants. The depot can look in the cage and at the flag, and Import billing own the flag, so the conflict goes to one of them with the urgency made plain.

review.note: Replying to the recipient leaves the billing-versus-depot contradiction with nobody who can settle it, leans on the depot's unconfirmed day-old flag to steer him off staying in, and tells him a depot query is being sent that this single message does not send.
